stem: Andrew is 14 years old and has chronic severe asthma. He prefers to use a Flixotide Accuhaler rather than a large-volume spacer. Which of the following is the correct first step in using an Accuhaler?

options.text: Open the device by holding the outer case and sliding the thumb grip away until it clicks
Shake the device vigorously before use
Breathe out fully into the mouthpiece
Press the lever after inhaling the dose
Rinse the mouth before loading the dose

explanation: The Accuhaler is a dry-powder inhaler. The first step is to open it by sliding the thumb grip until it clicks. It should not be shaken, and the patient should not breathe out into the mouthpiece.

citations.title: Practice Quiz: Asthma Management: Medications and Devices - Part B

rationale: This converts the original ordering task into a single-best-answer question focusing on the first correct step in Accuhaler use.

optionExplanations.A: Correct. The device is opened by sliding the thumb grip until it clicks, which prepares the dose for inhalation.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect. Dry-powder inhalers are not shaken before use.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect. The patient should breathe out away from the device, not into the mouthpiece.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect. The lever is used to load a dose before inhalation, not after.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect. Mouth rinsing is recommended after inhaling inhaled corticosteroid, not before loading the dose.

Instructions

Question 4 & 5 relate to this case

Asthma Management: Medications and Devices - Case 2

Andrew is 14 years old and has chronic severe asthma. He has had frequent hospital admissions, in addition to exercise-induced asthma and nocturnal symptoms most days. He uses salbutamol (Ventolin) most days.

He has been prescribed Ventolin (salbutamol) and Flixotide (fluticasone) via a large volume spacer (Volumatic), but does not take his medication regularly as he hates the spacer. When questioned, Andrew is unsure what medications he takes until prompted by his mother.
